details: The ongoing conflict between the US and Iran has seen further escalation, with the US sanctioning 10 entities for allegedly supporting Iran's military. President Trump denied plans to ease sanctions on Iran, contributing to a surge in oil prices. Amid this heightened geopolitical volatility, Bitcoin has notably risen by approximately 24% since hostilities began, outperforming traditional safe-haven assets like gold and silver. This suggests a growing perception among investors of Bitcoin as a digital safe haven during periods of global uncertainty.
title: US-Iran Tensions Escalate; Bitcoin Sees Safe Haven Demand

details: Australia's financial regulator, the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC), has set September 30, 2026, as the final deadline for cryptocurrency businesses to secure or vary an Australian Financial Services (AFS) license. Firms that fail to meet these authorization conditions by October 1 will face civil and criminal penalties, including potential fines amounting to 10% of their annual turnover. This marks a significant regulatory push to integrate digital asset businesses into existing financial services laws.
title: Australia Imposes September 30 Crypto Licensing Deadline

details: Global bond markets are experiencing a significant sell-off, with the UK government paying its highest interest rate on 10-year debt since 1999 at a recent auction. Similarly, US 30-year Treasury yields have risen to 5.6%, their highest level since 2002. This trend reflects a continued hawkish stance by central banks worldwide, including Australia's recent interest rate hike to a 15-year high, as they aim to combat persistent inflation. Rising borrowing costs generally lead to increased risk aversion across traditional financial markets.
title: Global Bond Yields Climb to Multi-Year Highs
